topics.title: Getting started
topics.summary: Build a factory, sell what it makes, and take the AI headquarters.

sections.heading: 1. Tap Ion
sections.text: Ion pays for research. Press 1 for the Extractor tool and click an Ion Crystal asteroid in your HQ cell; Ion flows straight into your stockpile. Your HQ's built-in solar panels power the first machines.

sections.heading: 2. Make something to sell
sections.text: Put an Extractor on an Iron Ore asteroid, a Refinery (2) next to it and a Sale Depot (4) nearby. Press B and drag belts from the extractor to the refinery and from the refinery to the depot. Iron Bars start selling.

sections.heading: 3. Grow the chain
sections.text: Assemblers (3) combine goods into more valuable ones. A Signal Relay needs an Iron Bar and a Copper Bar. Select any machine to choose its recipe.

sections.heading: 4. Research
sections.text: Select your Headquarters and press Research. New recipes, buildings and bonuses are discovered there, paid for with credits and Ion.

sections.heading: 5. Expand and win
sections.text: Claim cells with a unit, then deploy a Fort there from a Fort Construction Zone fed with Iron Plates and Copper Wire. Better craft need rare goods from those cells. Reach the sales target AND capture the AI headquarters.

topics.title: Ion power
topics.summary: The stockpile that pays for research.

sections.heading: Where it comes from
sections.text: An Extractor on an Ion Crystal asteroid adds Ion to your stockpile every cycle. Ion is never carried on belts.

sections.heading: What spends it
sections.text: Only research. Each research level costs credits and Ion. Machines, buildings and craft never use Ion.

sections.heading: Getting more
sections.text: Tap more Ion asteroids and research Ion Resonance to raise their yield. Ion Efficiency makes research cost less Ion.

topics.title: Power
topics.summary: Solar capacity that keeps your machines running.

sections.heading: Supply
sections.text: Your Headquarters has solar panels built in (20 MW). Each Solar Array adds 6 MW. Photovoltaics research raises all solar by 25%.

sections.heading: Demand
sections.text: Machines draw power only while working: Extractor 1 MW, Refinery and Water Purifier 2, Assembler 3, Shipyard 4. Depots, Storage, Forts and belts draw nothing.

sections.heading: Overloaded
sections.text: The top bar shows demand / supply and, in brackets, your spare power. When it goes negative, every machine slows to supply ÷ demand. Nothing stops outright.

sections.heading: More power
sections.text: Build Solar Arrays in free slots: 3 in your HQ cell, 2 in each Fort cell. More slots means holding more cells.

topics.title: Belts
topics.summary: One-way conveyors that carry goods between buildings.

sections.heading: Drawing
sections.text: Press B, then left-drag from a building across neighbouring tiles. Each step lays one one-way belt for a small credit cost. Drawing over your own belt the other way reverses it for free.

sections.heading: Splits and merges
sections.text: Start a drag on an existing belt to branch off it, or finish on one to merge into it. Mixed goods can share a belt; each belt step carries one item at a time.

sections.heading: Lanes and speed
sections.text: Each belt carries one item at a time, at its own speed. A busy asteroid can fill one belt: run a second belt out of the extractor to the same machine or Storage and items split between the lanes. Keeping each good on its own lane beats one long mixed belt.

sections.heading: Drone links between asteroids
sections.text: Each cell is its own asteroid, with open space between them, and belts stop at the edge. To move goods to another asteroid, research Drone Logistics and build Drone Pads: link a pad to a tile on another asteroid within range and a cargo drone carries goods across, one trip at a time. Shipping between asteroids is slow on purpose, so refine and assemble where the ore is and send finished goods. Select a link to see its flight time.

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.text: Click a belt to select it; its whole line (up to the next building or junction) lights up. Upgrade that belt or the whole line to Fast Conveyor (cyan), then Express Conveyor (gold). You pay per belt, and belts already at that speed are free.

sections.heading: Who gets what
sections.text: Machines pull the ingredients they need through any connected route. Machines and shipyards are always served before Storage and Sale Depots, so depots only sell surplus.

sections.heading: Removing
sections.text: Press X and drag across belts to dismantle them. Items on a removed belt are lost.

sections.heading: Belt View
sections.text: Press Belt View in the top bar (or V) when buildings hide your belts. Buildings fade and ignore clicks, so any click selects the belt there, and Dismantle only removes belts. Picking a building tool switches it off.

topics.title: Resource asteroids
topics.summary: Renewable deposits that Extractors mine.

sections.heading: Common
sections.text: Iron Ore, Copper Ore, Ice and Ion Crystal are found in every cell.

sections.heading: Rare
sections.text: Titanium Ore, Silicon Ore and Sulphur (gold glint) mine more slowly. Each HQ cell has one Silicon Ore asteroid; the rest sit in contested neutral cells.

sections.heading: Extra rare
sections.text: Unobtanium Ore, Complex Carbon and Gold Ore (gold halo) appear in a single cell each. Expect to fight for them.

sections.heading: Rich asteroids
sections.text: A gold ring marks a rich asteroid that mines faster than others of its kind. Asteroids never run out.

topics.title: Recipe tiers
topics.summary: Raw goods become bars, bars become components, components become assemblies.

sections.heading: Tier 1: refining
sections.text: Refineries turn each raw resource into a refined good: ore into bars, Ice into Water, Silicon Ore into Silicon Ingots, and so on.

sections.heading: Tier 2: components
sections.text: Assemblers turn refined goods into components such as Iron Plates, Copper Wire, Silicon Wafers and Titanium Struts. Water Purifiers make Purified Water.

sections.heading: Tier 3: assemblies
sections.text: Assemblers combine tier 1 and tier 2 goods into high-value assemblies like Electronics, Explosives and Reinforced Plate.

sections.heading: Unlocking
sections.text: Most components and assemblies must be researched first. A machine's recipe list shows how many recipes are still to discover.

topics.title: Extractor
topics.summary: Mines the asteroid it sits on.

sections.heading: Placing
sections.text: Press 1 and click an asteroid in a cell you own. One extractor per asteroid.

sections.heading: Output
sections.text: It mines three items per cycle into a small buffer, which connected machines pull from by belt. When the buffer cannot fit the next three it pauses until something takes its output.

sections.heading: Ion asteroids
sections.text: On an Ion Crystal, the extractor sends Ion straight to your stockpile instead; no belt needed.

topics.title: Refinery
topics.summary: Tier 1: turns a raw resource into a refined good.

sections.heading: Choosing a recipe
sections.text: Select the refinery and pick a recipe under Working on (for example Iron Bar from Iron Ore). It runs one recipe at a time; changing it resets progress.

sections.heading: What it needs
sections.text: A belt from an extractor (or storage) carrying the raw resource, power, and a belt out to whatever uses the result.

sections.heading: Reading it
sections.text: The Needs list shows each ingredient: green in stock, amber on the way, red missing. Floating icons over the machine show the same at a glance.

sections.heading: Filling up
sections.text: Machines order enough ingredients to fill their storage. Each machine's first batch comes first, so on a shared line every machine gets started before any one fills up.

topics.title: Assembler
topics.summary: Tier 2 and 3: combines goods into components and assemblies.

sections.heading: Choosing a recipe
sections.text: Select the assembler and pick a recipe under Working on. Recipes still locked behind research show which research unlocks them; others are still undiscovered.

sections.heading: What it needs
sections.text: Belts bringing every ingredient of the chosen recipe (two inputs can share one merged belt), power, and a belt out to a buyer, another machine, storage or a shipyard.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text: Wire and Wafer recipes make two items per cycle. If an assembler sits at 100%, it is waiting for room to put its output.

sections.heading: Filling up
sections.text: Machines order enough ingredients to fill their storage. Each machine's first batch comes first, so on a shared line every machine gets started before any one fills up.

topics.title: Water Purifier
topics.summary: Turns Water into Purified Water.

sections.heading: Unlocking
sections.text: Research Water Purification at your HQ.

sections.heading: Chain
sections.text: Ice asteroid, Extractor, Refinery set to Water, then a belt into the purifier. Purified Water sells well and goes into Coolant Cells.

topics.title: Sale Depot
topics.summary: Sells delivered goods for credits.

sections.heading: Selling
sections.text: Anything delivered is sold immediately at its price. Sales count toward the win target.

sections.heading: Sell list
sections.text: Select a depot to switch individual goods on or off, so it does not pull goods you would rather keep.

sections.heading: Priority
sections.text: Depots are served after machines and shipyards, so they only take surplus.

topics.title: Storage
topics.summary: A hub that collects surplus and supplies any connected machine.

sections.heading: Use
sections.text: Run several producer lines into one storage, then belts out to the machines that need the goods. It holds up to 40 items.

sections.heading: Accept list
sections.text: Select it to choose which goods it collects. Storages never feed each other.

topics.title: Shipyard
topics.summary: Builds craft from factory goods.

sections.heading: Ordering
sections.text: Select your shipyard and pick a craft under Working on. The order costs credits up front; craft whose parts you have not researched are marked and cannot be ordered yet.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.text: The shipyard pulls the craft's parts along belts, then launches it once every part has arrived and the build time has passed.

sections.heading: What each craft needs
sections.text: Mobile Guard (60): 4 Iron Plate + 2 Copper Wire. Tank (120): 2 Reinforced Plate + 1 Electronics. Artillery (150): 2 Explosives + 1 Reinforced Plate + 1 Electronics, so Sulphur and Complex Carbon. Strike Craft (220): 1 Hull Section + 1 Field Emitter + 1 Coolant Cell, so Titanium and Unobtanium.

sections.heading: Craft types
sections.text: Tank: holds the line against anything. Artillery: hits hardest but folds when hit back. Mobile Guard: a wall that punishes attackers, stronger as a cell's defender. Strike Craft: fast raider that flies over defended cells.

topics.title: Fort
topics.summary: Holds a cell and switches its factory on.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Outside your HQ cell, you can only build in a cell with a working Fort, and that cell's machines stop if the Fort is lost. An owned cell without a Fort or a unit reverts to neutral after a minute.

sections.heading: Getting one
sections.text: Forts are deployed from a Fort Construction Zone on the border of a neighbouring cell you hold. They cannot be placed directly.

sections.heading: Bonus
sections.text: A Fort cell has 2 Solar Array slots.

topics.title: Headquarters
topics.summary: Your base, your research office, and the target the AI is after.

sections.heading: Research
sections.text: Select it and press Research to open the research web.

sections.heading: Holding
sections.text: It holds its cell by itself and cannot be dismantled. Lose it and you lose the game; capture the AI's to win.

topics.title: Research
topics.summary: Discover recipes, buildings and bonuses at your HQ.

sections.heading: Opening
sections.text: Select your Headquarters and press Research. The game pauses while the web is open. Drag to pan and use the wheel to zoom.

sections.heading: Discovery
sections.text: Nodes you own or can buy show their names. A '?' outline is one step further out: buy what leads to it to reveal it. Anything further is hidden.

sections.heading: Costs
sections.text: Each level costs credits and Ion; Ion is spent on nothing else. Multi-level nodes stack their bonuses.

sections.heading: What you get
sections.text: New recipes and buildings, faster machines and extractors, cheaper Ion use, more Ion yield and better sale prices. The AI researches too.

topics.title: Territory
topics.summary: Claim cells for their asteroids, then hold them.

sections.heading: Claiming
sections.text: Select one of your craft and right-click a neutral cell. Arriving in a clear cell claims it after a short hold.

sections.heading: Holding
sections.text: Keep a unit there until a Fort is deployed from a construction zone next door. Unguarded cells revert to neutral after a minute; the grid pulses orange as a warning. Only cells with your HQ or a Fort can run machines.

sections.heading: Losing a cell
sections.text: If a cell is captured, its machines stop. Recapture it within three minutes to get them back; after that they are cleared.

topics.title: Craft and battles
topics.summary: Units that claim, defend and attack cells.

sections.heading: Moving
sections.text: Select a craft and right-click a cell. Hovering shows what the click will do: move, claim or attack.

sections.heading: Four stats
sections.text: Every craft fights on Attack, Reactive, Armour and HP. A hit does Attack minus the target's Armour (at least 1). If the target survives, it hits back with Reactive minus your Armour. Craft fight neighbouring cells only.

sections.heading: Damage falls with HP
sections.text: A damaged craft's Attack and Reactive shrink with its remaining HP, so attacking first matters and wounded craft hit back softer.

sections.heading: Battles
sections.text: Attacking a defended cell starts a turn-based battle and pauses the factory. Each side gets a few actions per turn: attack, move or hold the control point. Press Space to end your turn, or retreat.

sections.heading: Battle scenes
sections.text: Each attack plays a short scene: your formation and theirs, one ship per fifth of HP. Click to skip. Choose Off, Fast or Full under Battle scenes in the menu.

sections.heading: Defenders
sections.text: Each cell has one defender, which gets its defender bonus. When it falls, a reserve in the cell takes over.

topics.title: Credits and sales
topics.summary: Money for building, and the sales total you need to win.

sections.heading: Earning
sections.text: Every item a Sale Depot sells adds its price to your credits and to your sales total.

sections.heading: Spending
sections.text: Buildings, belts, craft orders and research cost credits. Spending never lowers your sales total. Dismantling refunds half a building's cost.

topics.title: Solar Array
topics.summary: Adds 6 MW of solar power.

sections.heading: Building it
sections.text: 80 credits plus 4 Copper Bars and 2 Silicon Ingots, taken from your Storage buildings when you place it. No belt needed.

sections.heading: Slots
sections.text: Each array needs a free slot: 3 in your HQ cell and 2 in each cell held by a Fort. Your HQ cell has a Silicon Ore asteroid, so you can make Silicon Ingots at home.

topics.title: Fort Construction Zone
topics.summary: Builds a Fort for the neighbouring cell, from goods your factory delivers.

sections.heading: Placing
sections.text: Put it on an edge tile of a cell you hold, facing the cell you want to expand into (not a corner). 150 credits.

sections.heading: Filling
sections.text: Belt in 6 Iron Plates and 4 Copper Wire from your local factory. The zone shows what it still needs.

sections.heading: Deploying
sections.text: Once it is full and you hold the neighbouring cell (claim it with a unit), the zone deploys a Fort there and disappears. That cell's factory comes online.

topics.title: Drone Pad
topics.summary: Sends goods to another of your asteroids by cargo drone.

sections.heading: Unlocking
sections.text: Research Drone Logistics (Logistics branch) to build Drone Pads. Belts stop at an asteroid's edge, so pads are the only way to move goods between asteroids.

sections.heading: Linking
sections.text: Select a pad: a ring shows its drone range. Press Link, then click a tile on another asteroid you hold inside the ring. A receiving pad is built there (or the link joins a pad already standing there). Each pad sends to one place; pick a new tile to relink, or Unlink. A pad can also pass goods on: link a receiving pad onward to reach further asteroids.

sections.heading: Belts
sections.text: Belt goods into the sending pad and belt them away from the receiving pad. Routes run through pads like junctions.

sections.heading: Drones
sections.text: The drone loads at the pad, flies across, drops its load and flies home before taking the next. Flight time grows with distance. Upgrade the link (select it) or research Drone Engines to fly faster, Cargo Drones to carry more per trip, and further Drone Logistics levels for more range.
